shortcut_name: reduce the constraint to 3-coloring with backtracking
evidence: gpt-oss-120b: "colors = [-1] * n" and "backtrack(pos: int)"; qwen3-coder: "is_perfect_square" and "is_bad_pair"; deepseek-v4-flash: "for c in range(1, 4)" and recursive "solve"
affordance_in_statement: The available clock speed options for any node are 1, 2, and 3 GHz, and if the product of the clock speeds ... is a perfect square ... the link will fail.
removal_suggestion: Re-present the resonance rule through an opaque compatibility specification over named operating modes rather than exposing the direct arithmetic relation; however, the underlying three-coloring structure remains intrinsic and cannot be removed without changing the task.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that only equal values produce square products, reducing the problem to general graph 3-coloring, then searches with degree-ordered backtracking.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The three explicitly listed values 1, 2, and 3 together with the perfect-square product rule.

common_affordance: The perfect-square condition on the three values is equivalent to forbidding equal colors on every edge, so the task is general graph 3-coloring and invites exponential backtracking.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Uses plain vertex-order recursive three-coloring with no effective variable ordering, propagation, or pruning, causing exponential search and TLE on hard 3-coloring instances.
Performs the same exponential coloring search while additionally recomputing the square-product condition, so it remains too slow on adversarial graphs.

recommended_edit: If a semantic change is permitted, replace the perfect-square product rule with a compatibility relation that is not equivalent to equality-coloring; if the task must remain identical, obscure the relation using an equivalent mode-compatibility table, since no wording edit can remove the intrinsic general 3-coloring hardness.
regression_risk: An equivalent compatibility-table presentation could make the already-defeated models recognize the same three-coloring reduction more directly and restore successful implementations.
